newsitem.title: USA: Steris drops on earnings warning.
newsitem.headline: Steris drops on earnings warning.

text.p: Shares of Steris Corp dropped about 25 percent after company warned its quarterly results would fall below Wall Street estimates, analysts said Wednesday.
Steris dropped 9-3/4 to 28-1/4 in midday trading.
Steris Chairman Bill Sanford said Wall Street's estimates were overly optimistic since many analysts did not accurately forecast results for AMSCO International Inc, which Steris acquired last year.
Sanford said AMSCO had unusually strong results for the December 1995 quarter and Wall Street had expected that performance to be repeated.

Steris, which makes cleaning and sterilization equipment for the healthcare industry, said it expects to earn about $13.5 million or $0.38 a share on sales of about $150 million for the third quarter ended December 31.
Analysts expected Steris to earn $0.53 a share in the third quarter, according to First Call, which tracks earnings estimates.
"It was a surprise to most people. The third quarter is normally their strongest quarter," said Vivian Wohl, an analyst with Robertson Stephens.

For the year ended March 31, the company expects earnings "in the mid $1.40s," excluding one-time merger-related charges. Fiscal 1997 sales are expected to be about $580 million to $590 million, Sanford said.
For Fiscal 1998, Sanford said he was comfortable with analysts' estimates of about $2 a share on sales of $700 million.
Elliott Schlang, an analyst who heads Lynch Jones & Ryan's Great Lakes Review and follows Steris, said Steris' sharp drop in share price was an overreaction.

"I think the stock is a buy," Schlang said. "We were at a buy to begin with, and we think it's currently a buy as well despite ... somewhat of a credibility problem" due to the earnings warning and subsequent stock price drop.
Schlang said he expects the lower-than-expected sales in AMSCO's repair/maintenance operations will be recovered in the fourth quarter.
"I think part of the sales disappointment in the third quarter, ending in December, will be made up in better than anticipated revenue in the March quarter," he said.
Schlang also lowered his earnings estimate for the year ending March 1997 to $1.48 a share from $1.55 versus last year's record $1.17 but maintained his $2.05 estimate for next year.
